series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.summary: "Brunei Darussalam's Intended Nationally Determined Contributions are summarised as follows: i. Energy sector: to reduce total energy consumption by 63% by 2035 compared to a Business-AsUsual (BAU) scenario; and to increase the share of renewables so that 10% of the total power generation is sourced from renewable energy by 2035 ii. Land Transport sector: to reduce carbon dioxide emissions from morning peak hour vehicle use by 40% by 2035 compared to a business as usual scenario. iii. Forestry sector: to increase the total gazette forest reserves to 55% of total land area, compared to the current levels of 41%." The INDC also includes an Adaptation contribution.

verdict.text: Brunei Darussalam pledges a 20% reduction by 2035 against 2035 business-as-usual (condition not read). The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2025-09-16. 47 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (1). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 15 MtCO₂e, DS-02 13.5 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: the pledge is 20% below a business-as-usual projection for 2035. That projection is not in any source loaded here, so the percentage cannot be turned into a tonnage and the trend cannot be judged against it. It submitted BTR1. 3 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 49.6 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 40% reduction in CO2 emissions from morning peak hour vehicle use by 2035 compared to the BAU scenario It was classed unconditional. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +0.93°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.41°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
